text.arabic_uthmani: سَيَقُولُ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا ٱنطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَىٰ مَغَانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ ۖ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُبَدِّلُوا۟ كَلَٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُل لَّن تَتَّبِعُونَا كَذَٰلِكُمْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ ۖ فَسَيَقُولُونَ بَلْ تَحْسُدُونَنَا ۚ بَلْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا

words.gloss_range: future-marked speech prediction introducing the ayah; singular VSO verb before a plural subject, with speech as the contested medium
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, assertion, and report; the local words activate controlled utterance rather than every possible speech register
words.prose: {{ar:سَيَقُولُ}} ({{tr:sayaqūlu}}) carries the future marker inside the speech verb, so the scene begins with anticipated utterance rather than later report. The singular preposed verb lets the speech event arrive before the plural speakers are named, while {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) threads this opening into the repeated speech architecture of the ayah and the same-surah reprise from 48:11.

topics.headline: predicted speech launches the discourse
topics.summary: future-marked speech prediction introducing the ayah; singular VSO verb before a plural subject, with speech as the contested medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens with speech already predicted and controlled before the speakers appear.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows converge on future marking, VSO singular-before-plural grammar, q-w-l speech semantics, the 48:11 same-surah recurrence, and the ayah-wide speech chain.

words.gloss_range: definite Form II passive participle naming the left-behind group; behindness and affected status are active, while broader succession senses remain background
words.root_gloss_range: behindness, being left, succession, and difference; the local passive participle narrows this to a defined left-behind group with oppositional coloring
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ}} ({{tr:al-mukhallafūna}}) is not a neutral crowd label: the definite passive participle presents a known group by their left-behind status. {{ar:خ ل ف}} ({{tr:kh-l-f}}) brings behindness, being left, and relational misalignment into the name, while the local form keeps the focus on affected status rather than proving who caused it.

topics.headline: left-behind status becomes a group identity
topics.summary: definite Form II passive participle naming the left-behind group; behindness and affected status are active, while broader succession senses remain background
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are introduced as a defined passive-participle class before their request is heard.
topics.reason: Rows about delayed nominative subject, Form II passive participle, definite plural class, behindness, recurrence around 48:11 and 48:16, and the 9:81 comparison survive with agency kept locally limited.

words.gloss_range: expected temporal condition introducing the moment that triggers the request
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the following perfect-form departure clause function as expected future time. The demand is therefore scoped to the moment when departure toward gains becomes live, so timing itself becomes part of the critique.

topics.headline: expected timing exposes opportunism
topics.summary: expected temporal condition introducing the moment that triggers the request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is timed to an expected departure, not floated as a timeless wish.
topics.reason: The rows agree that idhā with a perfect verb gives expected future time and that the temporal protasis scopes the later demand.

words.gloss_range: Form VII second-person plural departure; motion is local, with release-into-action pressure from the root family
words.root_gloss_range: release, loosening, separation, and setting out; the local Form VII narrows the branch to release into motion toward the expedition goal
words.prose: {{ar:ٱنطَلَقْتُمْ}} ({{tr:inṭalaqtum}}) is an intransitive departure completed by a goal phrase, and its second-person plural ending keeps the moving party distinct from the speakers. {{ar:ط ل ق}} ({{tr:ṭ-l-q}}) supplies release and unbinding imagery, but the local Form VII narrows that pressure to setting out into action rather than activating unrelated legal branches.

topics.headline: departure as release into motion
topics.summary: Form VII second-person plural departure; motion is local, with release-into-action pressure from the root family
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believers are the moving plural group, while the left-behind speakers try to attach themselves after that movement starts.
topics.reason: The rows support future force under idhā, intransitive movement to a goal, second-person plural marking, Form VII release-into-motion, and rarity of this motion form within the broader root family.

words.gloss_range: directional endpoint marker that makes the gains the destination of movement
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) marks the gains as the endpoint of the departure, not a vague direction. It places the desired object ahead and not yet possessed, then sets up the sequence from movement to goal to taking.

topics.headline: the goal is an endpoint, not scenery
topics.summary: directional endpoint marker that makes the gains the destination of movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the march is aimed at a named endpoint that explains the timing of the request.
topics.reason: Rows converge on ilā as goal marker, endpoint selection, not-yet-reached implication, and the structural slot between departure and taking.

words.gloss_range: indefinite broken plural for anticipated gains; material wealth and booty are active without requiring a specified prize already in hand
words.root_gloss_range: livestock wealth, booty, acquired advantage, and gain; the local plural narrows this to anticipated material gains as expedition objective
words.prose: {{ar:مَغَانِمَ}} ({{tr:maghānima}}) names the gains as an indefinite broken plural, so the attraction is an anticipated field of acquisition rather than a specific possession already in hand. {{ar:غ ن م}} ({{tr:gh-n-m}}) carries livestock wealth and seized-gain texture, and the word becomes the hinge between setting out, taking, and the later request to follow, with same-surah payoff in 48:19 and 48:20.

topics.headline: anticipated gains become the hinge
topics.summary: indefinite broken plural for anticipated gains; material wealth and booty are active without requiring a specified prize already in hand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the desired object is broad material gain, structurally placed between departure and taking.
topics.reason: The rows support prepositional governance, indefinite plural form, collective return-pronoun behavior, material wealth imagery, structural hinge placement, and forward links to 48:19 and 48:20.

words.gloss_range: purpose lām governing the following subjunctive action
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) functions as purpose lām and governs the following subjunctive verb. Its tight attachment makes acquisition the stated motive of the movement, which clarifies why the speakers wait for this moment.

topics.headline: purpose is fused to the taking
topics.summary: purpose lām governing the following subjunctive action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that taking is presented as the purpose of the movement, not merely a later possibility.
topics.reason: Rows identify lām al-taʿlīl, purpose governance of the subjunctive, and visible fusion to the taking verb.

words.gloss_range: purpose-governed taking with a feminine singular object pronoun referring back to the gains
words.root_gloss_range: taking, grasping, seizing, receiving, and holding; the local purpose verb selects concrete acquisition of the referenced gains
words.prose: {{ar:تَأْخُذُوهَا}} ({{tr:taʾkhudhūhā}}) is governed by the purpose marker and carries the object pronoun that locks the action back onto the gains. {{ar:أ خ ذ}} ({{tr:ʾ-kh-dh}}) can cover taking, seizing, and receiving, but the local clause narrows it to concrete acquisition, a field echoed in 48:19 and 48:20.

topics.headline: taking becomes concrete grasp
topics.summary: purpose-governed taking with a feminine singular object pronoun referring back to the gains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the goal is not abstract participation but grasping the gains as an object.
topics.reason: The rows support subjunctive governance, the object pronoun, concrete grasp semantics, broader taking range, and same-surah gain-taking echoes.

words.gloss_range: imperative request with first-person plural object; release/leave sense is narrowed to demanded permission for access
words.root_gloss_range: leaving, letting be, and release from restraint; the local imperative narrows this to a demand for permission or access
words.prose: {{ar:ذَرُونَا}} ({{tr:dharūnā}}) compresses a command and a beneficiary: the speakers order the addressees to leave or allow them. {{ar:ذ و ر}} ({{tr:dh-w-r}}) contributes release-from-restraint pressure, but the local imperative narrows it to a demand for permission to enter the expedition relationship.

topics.headline: permission is demanded as a command
topics.summary: imperative request with first-person plural object; release/leave sense is narrowed to demanded permission for access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the left-behind group phrases its access request as an imperative directed at the believers.
topics.reason: Rows support imperative addressee marking, the -nā object, defective-verb behavior, release/leave semantics, and the immediate answer by refusal of following.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form VIII following after an imperative, with the believers as object
words.root_gloss_range: following, tracking, pursuing, and attaching after; the local Form VIII narrows this to close following in the expedition relationship
words.prose: {{ar:نَتَّبِعْكُمْ}} ({{tr:nattabiʿkum}}) answers the preceding imperative in jussive form, making the proposed following depend on the granted request. {{ar:ت ب ع}} ({{tr:t-b-ʿ}}) keeps physical trailing and close pursuit visible, and the object ending points the following toward the believers before the relationship is later reversed and denied.

topics.headline: claimed following trails the expedition party
topics.summary: jussive Form VIII following after an imperative, with the believers as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proposed loyalty is grammatically dependent on permission and directed toward the believers.
topics.reason: Rows support jawāb al-ṭalab jussive syntax, object pronoun direction, Form VIII close following, assimilation, and mirror reversal with the later refusal.

words.gloss_range: directed desire taking a complement clause; root seeking imagery colors but does not replace local wanting
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, going after a target, and willing; the local Form IV narrows this to directed desire for an alteration clause
words.prose: {{ar:يُرِيدُونَ}} ({{tr:yurīdūna}}) introduces the inner motive and takes the following complement clause as its target. {{ar:ر و د}} ({{tr:r-w-d}}) brings seeking-after-a-target imagery into the desire, while local grammar keeps the sense as directed willing rather than physical roaming.

topics.headline: desire targets alteration
topics.summary: directed desire taking a complement clause; root seeking imagery colors but does not replace local wanting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah diagnoses an intention aimed specifically at changing the divine speech claim.
topics.reason: Rows support indicative desire with an plus subjunctive complement, directed wanting, the root image of seeking, Form IV narrowing, and continuity with desire language in 48:11.

words.gloss_range: complementizer turning the alteration clause into the object of wanting
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) converts the following action into complement content for the desire verb. That makes the intended alteration the object of wanting without inserting any softer intervening explanation.

topics.headline: the intended change is objectified
topics.summary: complementizer turning the alteration clause into the object of wanting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the desire is not vague; it is grammatically locked onto a proposed alteration.
topics.reason: Rows support an plus subjunctive as a noun-like complement, objectification of the alteration clause, and direct linkage between wanting and alteration.

words.gloss_range: Form II subjunctive alteration; substitution/change pressure is active but limited to attempted alteration of the stated divine speech object
words.root_gloss_range: exchange, substitution, replacement, and alteration; the local Form II narrows this to attempted alteration of a divine speech object
words.prose: {{ar:يُبَدِّلُوا۟}} ({{tr:yubaddilū}}) stands under the complement particle and names the intended act as Form II alteration. {{ar:ب د ل}} ({{tr:b-d-l}}) gives exchange and substitution force to the act, while local grammar keeps it focused on the specific speech object rather than every branch of change; the same field is later answered by no-change language in 48:23.

topics.headline: alteration is substitutional
topics.summary: Form II subjunctive alteration; substitution/change pressure is active but limited to attempted alteration of the stated divine speech object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the issue is not mere disagreement but an attempted replacement of what has been said.
topics.reason: Rows support subjunctive governance, Form II intensification, b-d-l substitution imagery, the qirāʾa shift to direct address as apparatus, comparison with 2:75, and 48:23 as later contrast.

words.gloss_range: singular abstract construct object of alteration; divine speech is selected, with the kalim variant kept as apparatus
words.root_gloss_range: speech, words, and the related wound-mark image; the local construct narrows this to divine speech as the object of attempted alteration
words.prose: {{ar:كَلَٰمَ}} ({{tr:kalāma}}) is the accusative object of attempted alteration and is bound in construct to the divine name. {{ar:ك ل م}} ({{tr:k-l-m}}) keeps speech and word-mark pressure active, while the local singular abstract form presents a unified speech object; the plural variant remains useful apparatus without replacing the main reading.

topics.headline: divine speech is the object at risk
topics.summary: singular abstract construct object of alteration; divine speech is selected, with the kalim variant kept as apparatus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proposed alteration targets speech bound to God, not merely a human instruction.
topics.reason: Rows support object grammar, construct binding, contrast with the q-w-l chain, speech/wound semantic pressure, the kalim variant, and the 2:75 divine-speech distortion parallel.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name as second term of the construct; deity-source force is active, while later nominative role is separate
words.root_gloss_range: the divine-name field, with worship and deity as the relevant range; the local case role determines whether the name marks source or speaker
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) completes the construct phrase in genitive case, making the speech object divine in source and authority. {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) keeps the divine-name field live, but the local payoff is the genitive source role, later contrasted with the nominative speaker role.

topics.headline: the speech is marked as God’s
topics.summary: genitive divine name as second term of the construct; deity-source force is active, while later nominative role is separate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attempted change is framed as interference with speech belonging to God.
topics.reason: Rows support genitive iḍāfa role, proper divine name definitizing the phrase, source authority, derivational dispute kept as background, and contrast with the later nominative occurrence.

words.gloss_range: second-person masculine singular imperative commanding the Prophet to relay counter-speech
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, assertion, and report; the local words activate controlled utterance rather than every possible speech register
words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) is a compressed imperative to the Prophet, turning the discourse from predicted human speech into commanded counter-speech. {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) connects this pivot to the ayah-wide q-w-l chain: human prediction, prophetic command, completed divine saying, and later human retort.

topics.headline: commanded counter-speech interrupts
topics.summary: second-person masculine singular imperative commanding the Prophet to relay counter-speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer is not spontaneous human rebuttal but a commanded prophetic relay.
topics.reason: Rows support second masculine singular imperative, relay function, discourse pivot, q-w-l chain placement, and same-surah contrasts including 48:23 and 48:26.

words.gloss_range: categorical future negation governing the following subjunctive follow-verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَّن}} ({{tr:lan}}) gives emphatic future denial and governs the following subjunctive. Its position before the mirrored follow verb makes the refusal categorical, answering their hoped-for access in the same future register.

topics.headline: future following is categorically denied
topics.summary: categorical future negation governing the following subjunctive follow-verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal directly shuts the future door opened by their request to follow.
topics.reason: Rows support lan as emphatic future negation, governance of the mirrored follow verb, and direct opposition to the speakers’ hope.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII following denied under future negation, with object pronouns reversing the earlier proposal
words.root_gloss_range: following, tracking, pursuing, and attaching after; the local Form VIII narrows this to close following in the expedition relationship
words.prose: {{ar:تَتَّبِعُونَا}} ({{tr:tattabiʿūnā}}) repeats the same following field under the negator, but now the pronouns reverse the earlier direction. {{ar:ت ب ع}} ({{tr:t-b-ʿ}}) preserves the tracking and close-following image, while the grammar denies exactly the relationship the speakers proposed.

topics.headline: the following relation is reversed and refused
topics.summary: Form VIII following denied under future negation, with object pronouns reversing the earlier proposal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal mirrors their own following-language while flipping who would follow whom.
topics.reason: Rows support lan-governed subjunctive, Form VIII pursuit, second-person plural subject, first-person object, pronoun reversal, and convergence of request-form with negation.

words.gloss_range: comparison particle linking the refusal to the prior divine statement
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) sets up a manner-link between the refusal and what was said before. It bridges the commanded reply to the authority clause, so the human exclusion is framed as accordance with prior divine speech.

topics.headline: manner-link binds refusal to authority
topics.summary: comparison particle linking the refusal to the prior divine statement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal is presented as matching a prior divine statement, not as a fresh tactical decision.
topics.reason: Rows support kāf comparison/manner force, linkage between refusal and prior decree, and the bridge between the command and the divine saying clause.

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative with second-person plural suffix applying the prior decree directly to the addressed group
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكُمْ}} ({{tr:dhālikum}}) combines distal reference with a second-person plural suffix. The effect is pointed: what was said before is not vague background, but a decree applied directly to the addressed group.

topics.headline: the prior decree is pointed at them
topics.summary: distal demonstrative with second-person plural suffix applying the prior decree directly to the addressed group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative is both distancing and directly addressed to the group being refused.
topics.reason: Rows support demonstrative complement function, distal reference, -kum addressee force, and the structural bridge to the divine saying clause.

words.gloss_range: perfect speech verb grounding the command in completed divine saying
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, assertion, and report; the local words activate controlled utterance rather than every possible speech register
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) shifts the speech chain from future human claims and present command to completed declaration. {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) keeps the same speech medium active, but the perfect form grounds the refusal in prior divine speech.

topics.headline: completed saying grounds the refusal
topics.summary: perfect speech verb grounding the command in completed divine saying
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Prophet’s refusal is backed by a completed divine saying rather than by present negotiation.
topics.reason: Rows support perfect qāla after imperative qul, completed declaration semantics, contrast with future say forms, and its third q-w-l position.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name as explicit subject of the completed saying
words.root_gloss_range: the divine-name field, with worship and deity as the relevant range; the local case role determines whether the name marks source or speaker
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) is nominative and explicit as the subject of the completed saying. {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) keeps the divine-name authority field present, and the case shift from the earlier genitive occurrence moves from divine source of speech to divine speaker.

topics.headline: God is named as speaker
topics.summary: nominative divine name as explicit subject of the completed saying
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the authority clause names God explicitly as the speaker, preventing the refusal from sounding merely human.
topics.reason: Rows support nominative agent role, explicit divine subject, contrast with genitive source role, central placement in the speech frame, and second occurrence of the divine name.

words.gloss_range: preposition forming a temporal source phrase with the following before-word
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) joins the following time-word to form a temporal source phrase. Here its source force is not partitive but prior, grounding the refusal in what has already been said.

topics.headline: the source is prior time
topics.summary: preposition forming a temporal source phrase with the following before-word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal reaches back to prior authority instead of reacting only to the current request.
topics.reason: Rows support min plus qablu as temporal source, temporal origin rather than partitive source, and authority-from-before force.

words.gloss_range: adverbial before-word with omitted complement; facing/acceptance branches remain background to prior-time meaning
words.root_gloss_range: before, facing, receiving, and accepting; the local adverbial phrase narrows this to prior time and precedent
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلُ}} ({{tr:qablu}}) closes the temporal phrase as an adverbial before-word with its complement left implicit. {{ar:ق ب ل}} ({{tr:q-b-l}}) can range through before, facing, and acceptance, but the local form selects prior time and precedent.

topics.headline: beforehand closes the authority phrase
topics.summary: adverbial before-word with omitted complement; facing/acceptance branches remain background to prior-time meaning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine saying is placed before the current request, making the refusal preexisting rather than improvised.
topics.reason: Rows support qablu with omitted complement, fixed final vowel behavior, before-time meaning, broader q-b-l range, and recurrence of the min qablu formula around divine precedent.

words.gloss_range: sequential conjunction tying the predicted retort to the refusal
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) resumes and sequences the retort after the refusal. Its attachment to the next future speech frame keeps the dialogue continuous and marks the accusation as the next move in the same exchange.

topics.headline: the retort follows as consequence
topics.summary: sequential conjunction tying the predicted retort to the refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the next accusation is sequenced as the predictable consequence of refusal, not a new independent scene.
topics.reason: Rows support fa as narrative sequencer, consequence marker after refusal, attachment to the second future speech verb, and continuity rather than a new scene.

words.gloss_range: plural future speech verb returning the opening q-w-l frame after the refusal
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, assertion, and report; the local words activate controlled utterance rather than every possible speech register
words.prose: {{ar:سَيَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:sayaqūlūna}}) returns to future human speech after the commanded refusal, now in plural form. {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) marks this as the fourth speech movement in the ayah, and the repeated future frame turns the counter-accusation into another predicted move rather than a surprise.

topics.headline: predicted counter-speech returns
topics.summary: plural future speech verb returning the opening q-w-l frame after the refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening future-speech frame comes back as a plural retort after the refusal.
topics.reason: Rows support plural future verb, pro-drop subject, counter-accusation function, sequence plus futurity from the preceding conjunction, and the four-part q-w-l architecture.

words.gloss_range: first adversative correction particle used by the left-behind group to reframe the refusal as envy
words.prose: {{ar:بَلْ}} ({{tr:bal}}) introduces the group’s attempted correction: they pivot from the refusal to a counter-framing that blames envy. The first occurrence matters because a second occurrence will override it, creating a correction-over-correction structure.

topics.headline: human correction deflects blame
topics.summary: first adversative correction particle used by the left-behind group to reframe the refusal as envy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers try to replace the divine framing with their own accusation.
topics.reason: Rows support iḍrāb, human deflection from the prior framing, envy accusation, and later answer by the second bal.

words.gloss_range: direct second-person-to-first-person envy accusation; deprivation-envy is active, with qirāʾāt showing pronoun and vowel pressure as apparatus
words.root_gloss_range: envy that wishes deprivation, not neutral desire for a similar benefit; the local accusation selects hostile zero-sum envy
words.prose: {{ar:تَحْسُدُونَنَا}} ({{tr:taḥsudūnanā}}) fuses second-person plural subject marking with a first-person plural object, making the accusation confrontational. {{ar:ح س د}} ({{tr:ḥ-s-d}}) selects envy as wishing deprivation of another’s blessing rather than neutral desire, while the variant readings show pressure around stem vowel and person without displacing the local direct address.

topics.headline: envy is made confrontational
topics.summary: direct second-person-to-first-person envy accusation; deprivation-envy is active, with qirāʾāt showing pronoun and vowel pressure as apparatus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation is not generic resentment but a direct you-to-us charge of deprivation-envy.
topics.reason: Rows support direct subject-object morphology, ḥasad versus ghibṭa, zero-sum deprivation valence, variant readings, 4:54 and 2:109 envy contexts, and rarity of the envy lexeme.

words.gloss_range: second adversative correction particle overriding the human counter-claim
words.prose: {{ar:بَلْ}} ({{tr:bal}}) is the second corrective turn, and it does not continue the human accusation. It cancels the envy explanation and replaces it with the diagnosis of deficient understanding, so the repeated particle stages rival corrections.

topics.headline: divine correction overrides their correction
topics.summary: second adversative correction particle overriding the human counter-claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrative answers their attempted reframing with a stronger corrective turn.
topics.reason: Rows support the second bal as narrator/divine correction, cancellation of the first bal, replacement of envy with comprehension diagnosis, and paired bal structure.

words.gloss_range: auxiliary perfect with imperfect negated verb creating a habitual state diagnosis
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and state; the local auxiliary narrows this to an ongoing condition attached to the group
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) turns the closing diagnosis into a state attached to the group. {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) contributes being and condition, while the auxiliary plus imperfect construction makes their non-understanding habitual rather than momentary.

topics.headline: non-understanding is chronic
topics.summary: auxiliary perfect with imperfect negated verb creating a habitual state diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing fault is framed as an ongoing condition, not a one-time misunderstanding.
topics.reason: Rows support kāna plus imperfect as past habitual, state-of-being semantics, plural subject continuity, and same-surah state-formula echoes.

words.gloss_range: negation inside the state construction, later restricted by exception
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) supplies the negative core of the closing diagnosis inside the state construction. Yet it also prepares the later exception, so the verdict becomes calibrated rather than absolute nothingness.

topics.headline: negation prepares a measured verdict
topics.summary: negation inside the state construction, later restricted by exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation is strong but not final, because the exception will measure what remains.
topics.reason: Rows support negation of the understanding verb, embedding in the kāna complex, chronic negative force, and later restriction by exception plus measure.

words.gloss_range: imperfect plural verb for deep understanding; locally intransitive and negated within the chronic diagnosis
words.root_gloss_range: penetrating understanding and deep grasp; the local negated imperfect narrows this to an ongoing failure to grasp the meaning beneath events
words.prose: {{ar:يَفْقَهُونَ}} ({{tr:yafqahūna}}) names ongoing understanding within the negated state frame. {{ar:ف ق ه}} ({{tr:f-q-h}}) reaches deeper than surface knowing toward penetrating grasp, while the local intransitive use makes the failure general: they do not get beneath the refusal and the gains.

topics.headline: the issue is failed deep grasp
topics.summary: imperfect plural verb for deep understanding; locally intransitive and negated within the chronic diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing diagnosis concerns failure to penetrate meaning, not lack of information about spoils alone.
topics.reason: Rows support imperfect ongoing action, plural subject continuity, local intransitivity, fiqh as deep penetration, 9:81 pairing with left-behind people, and closure of the speech contest as comprehension failure.

words.gloss_range: exception particle carving out a small remainder after negated understanding

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative measure of understanding; scarcity image quantifies the residual grasp

words.prose: {{ar:قَلِيلًۭا}} ({{tr:qalīlan}}) lands as an indefinite accusative measure, quantifying the understanding itself. {{ar:ق ل ل}} ({{tr:q-l-l}}) gives scarcity and diminishment to the residue: the closing verdict is not no comprehension at all, but a slight, insufficient grasp, with deficient-comprehension parallels such as 4:78.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence from the left-behind, through departure, to gains, taking, and the doubled language of following.
baseline_models.mechanism: A rear-positioned group waits until an unimpeded movement toward acquisition becomes visible, then asks to attach itself to the route. The answering prohibition preserves the distinction between bearing the earlier path and joining only its yield-bearing end.

activation_trace.role: Rear-positioning makes their designation a spatial and temporal relation to the movement they missed.
Release without confinement marks the moment when the route toward gain visibly opens.
Successful acquisition supplies the requested route's terminal yield.
Taking into possession identifies the terminal act they seek to share.
Leaving or allowing turns their desired attachment into a request for permission.
Trailing after another supplies both the proposed attachment and its explicit refusal.

changed_reading.before: They ask to accompany a later expedition for spoils and are refused.
changed_reading.after: They try to splice themselves into a yield-producing sequence only after its costly front and rear have been fixed; the refusal denies retroactive attachment, not movement in the abstract.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Four turns of saying surround the wish to substitute God's communicative act and the appeal to what was said before.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah stages an attempted renegotiation. A request is forecast, its operative aim is exposed as substitution, an authorized reply closes the negotiation by invoking prior speech, and an envy charge tries to redescribe authoritative allocation as private emotion.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation in an affair organizes the four utterances as bids and counter-bids rather than incidental dialogue.
Substitution supplies the operative attempt to put a new participation rule in the place of the prior one.
Intelligible speech connecting parties makes the word a live social relation with consequences.
Temporal precedence makes the invoked saying prior to, and therefore regulative of, the present request.
The accusation of wanting another's advantage removed recodes a rule-bound refusal as rivalry over possession.

changed_reading.before: They want to alter a divine statement about who may join.
changed_reading.after: They try to alter effective speech by changing the social performance it governs; when the authorized counter-speech blocks that substitution, they offer an affective counter-explanation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Their wanting, repeated speech, envy allegation, and final diagnosis of little understanding.
baseline_models.mechanism: Gain-seeking cycles through request, blocked request, and accusation. The last correction does not merely label ignorance; it exposes a compression error in which a prior causal rule is reduced to another party's supposed scarcity emotion.

activation_trace.role: Seeking and scouting for a desired object drives the sequence beyond a neutral wish.
The split-root image of repetition and hesitation gives the request-refusal-accusation sequence a looping shape.
Abundant saying contrasts with the small amount of understanding named at the close.
The non-removal branch keeps open a weaker possibility: their charge may describe covetous comparison more than destructive envy.
Grasping a thing's sense supplies the missing capacity needed to connect sequence, speech, and outcome.
Smallness limits that grasp rather than merely reporting a low stock of information.

changed_reading.before: They misunderstand the refusal and accuse the others of envy.
changed_reading.after: Their many strategic sayings are generated by a desire-loop that cannot hold the larger causal structure, so it repeatedly shrinks ordered exclusion into interpersonal jealousy.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The collision between following and the phrase that God said it from before.
baseline_models.mechanism: Precedence is also activated as facing. The prior saying stands at the front of the route and gives following its orientation; attaching at the tail while bypassing that front-facing condition is not the same act of following.

activation_trace.role: Facing one thing with another spatializes the prior word as the front toward which valid movement is oriented.
Temporal advance anchors that orientation in an earlier determination.
Ordered succession makes following depend on where one enters the sequence.
Effective saying distinguishes the governing utterance from the rival utterances around it.

changed_reading.before: The refusal is justified because God said so earlier.
changed_reading.after: The earlier saying is the route's orienting front: one cannot count as following by entering only behind the present gain while bypassing the prior direction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier sequence locates increase inside settled hearts: tranquility is delivered, movement subsides into stability, and faith grows. Against that economy, the focus speakers measure increase by exterior acquisitions and taking, so their little understanding becomes a confusion about what kind of increase the surah is producing.

activation_trace.role: External acquisition supplies the focus group's preferred measure of increase.
Understanding anchors the revised diagnosis as a failure to distinguish two economies of increase.
Delivery from outside supplies tranquility as a received input rather than seized property.
A locus of stability makes settled interiority the condition of the increase.
The heart locates the transformation in the interior rather than in captured goods.
Growth names the alternative accumulation that the focus speakers fail to count.

structural_cues: 48:4 makes tranquility in hearts the means by which faith is added to faith.
48:15 instead clusters gain, taking, desire, and little understanding.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two explicit forms of addition; I infer that their juxtaposition diagnoses a wrong metric of increase. They may remain parallel rewards rather than an intended contrast.

changed_reading.before: They understand too little to accept exclusion from material gain.
changed_reading.after: They count increase only when it can be taken, while the surrounding sequence treats stable inward growth as the prior and more decisive gain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding pledge has exchange-like form but covenantal content: obedience is pledged, a tightened bond can be undone, a preserved compact can be fulfilled without deficit, and reward follows. The late request in 48:15 therefore resembles a demand to enter on the dividend side of a compact whose risk-bearing side was not kept.

activation_trace.role: Ordered succession anchors the disputed question of entering after, rather than through, the covenantal sequence.
Acquired benefit supplies the dividend-like end of the analogy.
A pledge of obedience establishes the compact to which later benefit can be related.
Undoing a firmly made covenant supplies the excluded breach-side of the transaction.
Completion without deficit links preserved commitment to its full consequence.
A safeguarded compact gives the prior relation durable rather than opportunistic form.

structural_cues: 48:10 orders pledge, possible breach, fulfillment, and reward before the late-following request of 48:15.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies compact, breach, fulfillment, and reward; I supply the arrow from that architecture to the later allocation dispute. The two scenes could instead be adjacent but administratively distinct.

changed_reading.before: The request concerns permission to join a profitable march.
changed_reading.after: The request seeks retroactive access to a covenant's return after bypassing the commitment that generated it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding portrait separates tongue-output from heart-content in the same left-behind speakers. The four speech turns in 48:15 can therefore be read as successive verbal instruments: excuse, request, official refusal, and accusation, with the last utterance counterfeiting an affective motive for a rule it cannot displace.

activation_trace.role: Negotiating speech gives the focus sequence its tactical verbal form.
The envy charge supplies the final counterfeit motive offered after the request is blocked.
Unvoiced inner saying sharpens the explicit gap between what is spoken and what remains in the self.
The speech-organ makes outward production separable from inward commitment.
The false-speaker branch keeps deliberate verbal counterfeiting live rather than treating the mismatch as mere confusion.
The heart provides the withheld interior against which their produced explanations are measured.

structural_cues: 48:11 and 48:15 name the same left-behind group and repeat forecast speech, command speech, and concealed motive.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet directly supplies the mouth-heart split; I infer that the later envy allegation continues the same speech strategy. A live alternative is that the later charge is sincere despite the earlier dissimulation.

changed_reading.before: Their envy charge is simply an incorrect explanation of the refusal.
changed_reading.after: The charge is a second-order verbal instrument that tries to counterfeit the refusal's motive after direct renegotiation fails.

context_deltas.mechanism: The left-behind had treated non-return as the expected outcome, beautified that forecast inwardly, and became a ruined or stagnant people. Their later rush toward gain is a reversal after the forecast fails. The envy accusation then hides not only disobedience but a badly priced wager on who would return with value.

activation_trace.role: Remaining at the rear is recast as the position produced by their failed forecast.
The envy allegation deflects attention from the requesters' own reversed valuation.
An outcome whose end cannot be trusted supplies the speculative basis of their choice.
Return and turning supply both the event they denied and the reversal their later request performs.
Making the forecast appear attractive explains why the bad wager could govern action.
Stagnation until corruption supports the economic dead-end produced by their forecast.

structural_cues: 48:12 attributes to them a confident non-return forecast before 48:15 presents their attempt to join the returned group's gain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies forecast, inward beautification, return, and later demand; I supply the wager and repricing analogy. The bad expectation may be a moral diagnosis without an economic mechanism.

changed_reading.before: They opportunistically seek spoils after staying behind.
changed_reading.after: They try to reverse a failed wager on the community's non-return, then redescribe the resulting allocation loss as envy rather than as the consequence of their own forecast.

context_deltas.mechanism: The very group barred from the present gain is subsequently called into a costly encounter and offered reward through obedience. The refusal in 48:15 is therefore sequence-specific rather than caste-like: access reopens prospectively through burden-bearing action, but not retroactively at the profitable endpoint.

activation_trace.role: Their current rear position is the status that the later call tests rather than freezes forever.
Catching up is denied for this gain but remains conceptually distinct from answering a future call.
A direct summons reopens a forward route for the previously excluded group.
Mutual combat gives that reopened route real cost and exposure.
Obedient yielding supplies the prospective condition of inclusion.
Compensation for work restores a reward path without reallocating the earlier gain.

structural_cues: 48:16 addresses the left-behind directly and makes future reward conditional on a new costly response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the later call and conditional reward; I infer that it limits the scope of the earlier prohibition. The later campaign may be a separate test without formally defining the first refusal.

changed_reading.before: You will never be allowed to follow us because you belong to an excluded group.
changed_reading.after: You cannot enter this completed reward-chain at its end, but a new cost-bearing chain will call you and can generate its own reward.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet repeats the focus ayah's exact gain-and-taking pair, but embeds it in a chain of pledge, known interior state, settled tranquility, returned recompense, and promise. To change the word is thus to extract gain and taking from the relational bundle that specifies how and to whom they arrive.

activation_trace.role: Changing a thing's form becomes the attempted extraction of two attractive terms from their larger sequence.
A meaningful expression can carry a whole arrangement even when the request isolates only its gain-bearing portion.
The obedience pledge supplies the embodied relation preceding the reward.
Settled stability supplies an interior consequence of that relation before material yield appears.
Reward returning to its worker gives the gain a causal route back to prior action.
The same acquired benefit as in the focus is now attached to the preceding pledge sequence.
The same taking event confirms that the context is specifying the focus ayah's contested yield.
A spoken promise opens expectation while retaining control over its recipient and fulfillment.

structural_cues: 48:18-20 moves without interruption from pledge and known hearts to tranquility, recompense, gains, taking, and promise.
48:15 repeats gains and taking but proposes a different set of followers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the contiguous bundle and exact lexical recurrence; I infer that substitution means detaching the payoff from that bundle and reassigning it. A narrower reading would treat the word as only a discrete prior prohibition.

changed_reading.before: They want the content of a divine statement changed.
changed_reading.after: They want the gain-and-taking segment cut out of a pledged causal bundle and reattached to late followers, thereby changing the word's enacted form.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context differentiates what is hastened now, what is beyond present capacity yet already encompassed, and a nearer opening placed short of a later promised entry. Refusal at one phase is therefore not evidence of scarce goodwill. The envy claim mistakes staged access for possessive withholding.

activation_trace.role: What comes earlier anchors the focus refusal in a temporal order rather than a timeless aversion.
The scarcity diagnosis is the reading that phased access destabilizes.
Acceleration and bringing forward mark one allocation as deliberately early.
Effective capacity distinguishes present inability from permanent exclusion.
Complete encompassing in knowledge and control keeps the unavailable outcome inside a larger schedule.
Nearness short of the endpoint supplies an intervening event rather than the final goal.
An opening that begins what follows turns the near event into a temporal gateway.
Temporal nearness locates that gateway before the farther fulfillment.

structural_cues: 48:20 calls one gain hastened; 48:21 names another beyond present capacity but encompassed.
48:27 places a near opening before a later safe entry and explicitly contrasts divine knowledge with human non-knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies multiple phased fulfillments; I infer a common scheduling logic that explains the focus refusal. The promises may have distinct referents whose temporal structures should not be fully merged.

changed_reading.before: The insiders refuse to share a finite opportunity and are accused of envy.
changed_reading.after: The refusal guards a phase boundary in a staged fulfillment; envy is a low-resolution reading that confuses not-yet or not-this-chain with never.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding gain sequence twice defines divine action by restraining hands, and the second restraint occurs after granting victory. Victory can therefore consist in controlled non-taking. The focus speakers isolate spoils and possession as the only intelligible success, while the packet treats withheld force as part of success itself.

activation_trace.role: Possessive taking anchors the narrow victory metric that the context reverses.
The envy charge assumes that withholding can only express rival possession.
Active prevention makes restraint a positive component of the promised outcome.
The hand as force identifies the capacity being withheld rather than an absence of capacity.
Reciprocal prevention repeats the restraint mechanism on both sides.
Concrete hands make non-seizure bodily and reciprocal rather than merely rhetorical.
Victory explicitly precedes or accompanies restraint, proving that conquest need not be maximized taking.

structural_cues: 48:20 joins promised gains to restrained hands; 48:24 joins granted victory to mutual hand-restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies restraint inside victory; I infer that 48:15's blocked following protects this broader success metric. The restraint passages may govern other encounters without directly motivating the spoil allocation.

changed_reading.before: The dispute is over who gets to take the spoils.
changed_reading.after: The deeper dispute is over whether taking exhausts the meaning of victory; the refusal belongs to an order in which disciplined non-taking can itself be the decisive gain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later lexical echo moves substitution from a single utterance to a recurrent path: no replacement is found for God's running way. The word in 48:15 can therefore function as an executable pattern linking prior response to later outcome, not merely as a sentence whose wording must remain intact.

activation_trace.role: Communicative connection anchors the divine word as the expressed side of the pattern.
Putting one thing in another's place names the focus group's attempted rerouting.
Tracing one step after another makes participation in a path the enacted side of the word.
A running, followed way expands the divine determination into a recurrent causal path.
The explicit denial of substitution mirrors the focus attempt and closes the path-level rerouting.

structural_cues: 48:15 says they want substitution in God's word; 48:23 says no substitution will be found in God's running way.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact substitution root and divine attribution in both clauses; I infer that word and running way are two scales of one executable order. They may instead be separate determinations linked only rhetorically.

changed_reading.before: They attempt to contradict a prior divine statement.
changed_reading.after: They attempt to reroute a followed causal path so that a different antecedent produces the same outcome, but the path is as resistant to substitution as the utterance.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later blocked advance is explained by bodies unknown to the advancing group: pressure could trample them and stain the actors, while separation would change what action was possible. This activates a protective reading of the focus boundary. A denied attachment can preserve unseen relations and prevent indiscriminate pressure, not merely reserve goods.

activation_trace.role: Catching up anchors the controlled movement whose added participants could change pressure on the route.
The bodily injury branch keeps hidden harm inside the semantic field of the word being protected.
Crushing pressure supplies the concrete harm that an apparently frustrating delay prevents.
A contaminating stain makes unintended injury feed back onto those producing it.
Separation and discrimination determine when force can act without striking the concealed persons.

structural_cues: 48:25 makes non-advance depend on unknown intermixture and says a different action would follow if the groups separated.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a protective delay elsewhere; I infer that the focus prohibition may share its boundary-management logic. The later scene may explain only the earlier ceasefire and should not be asserted as the direct cause of 48:15's refusal.

changed_reading.before: Exclusion protects the insiders' share from opportunists.
changed_reading.after: Exclusion may also protect a route and its unseen bodies from the distortions or injuries caused by attaching an untested group at the moment of taking.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet opposes heated group pride and impulsive unknowing to descending tranquility and a protective word affixed by judgment. This changes divine speech from information outside the group into a binding criterion carried by it. The focus group's desired substitution would unstick that criterion, while its envy charge redescribes disciplined binding as hostile group heat.

activation_trace.role: Changing form anchors the attempt to loosen or reshape the governing criterion.
Meaningful speech supplies the criterion's articulated form.
Heated pride supplies the rival mode of group cohesion and interpretation.
Impulsive instability links unknowing to affective heat rather than mere missing data.
Cessation of agitation supplies the counter-condition in which the binding word can be borne.
Affixing by judgment turns the word into an adhered norm rather than detachable information.
The shared speech root links the later affixed criterion to the focus ayah's threatened word.
Protective deflection gives the adhered word a harm-regulating function.

structural_cues: 48:26 sequences heated pride, ignorance, tranquility, affixing, the protective word, and worthiness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a later word from the same root that is affixed to the believers; I infer that it reveals how divine speech can bind conduct in 48:15. The later word need not be the same utterance as the earlier word.

changed_reading.before: God's word is an external statement the requesters want revised.
changed_reading.after: The word is also an adhered protective criterion; admitting a payoff-only attachment would change how that criterion holds the group together.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final plant sequence models belonging as emergence around an origin, reciprocal strengthening, thickening after delicacy, and standing on supporting stems. Against it, the focus request seeks attachment only when harvest-like gain is available. The refusal can preserve developmental continuity: members are not interchangeable late additions to yield but participants in the process that made the body stand.

activation_trace.role: Coming after and standing in another's place supplies the late-succession problem tested by the plant model.
Late catching-up anchors the contrast with growth through the whole developmental sequence.
Covetous admiration without removal keeps the requesters' desire to share another group's maturity distinct from destructive envy.
Cultivated growth supplies the long causal process behind the community's visible result.
A shoot emerging around the origin models new membership as organic outgrowth rather than external docking.
Plants strengthening one another makes mutual support constitutive of maturation.
Thickening after delicacy supplies accumulated resilience rather than instant entitlement.
Completed uprightness marks the mature state produced by the preceding stages.
Supporting stems carry the mature body and preserve the memory of what bears its weight.
Inward anger caused by visible growth distinguishes an outsider's reaction from the focus group's accusation of envy.

structural_cues: 48:29 gives an ordered biological sequence before naming the affect it produces in opponents.
48:15 asks for following precisely when acquisitions are ready to be taken.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the plant sequence and the late request; I map development onto membership and gain onto harvest. The plant may characterize the community generally without adjudicating this particular request.

changed_reading.before: They are denied a share because they did not accompany the earlier expedition.
changed_reading.after: They seek harvest-time attachment to an organism they did not help strengthen; the refusal protects process-grown membership rather than treating people as swappable recipients of yield.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The bodily branch of the speech root is surprising and should not replace its ordinary communicative force. It remains anchored in the focus word itself and in the trace-following construction; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for an embodied cost that late substitution would overwrite.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The threatened change to God's word beside the doubled following construction.

changed_reading.before: Changing the word means changing a communicated allocation.
changed_reading.after: The requested late attachment would also overwrite an embodied scar-map of who traversed the earlier path and bore its cut.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading activates remote material branches under the request verb and is therefore deliberately strange. It remains anchored in the exact request, rear-position, and following roots; render it as a severance-and-graft image, not as the lexical translation of the imperative.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The left-behind say, in effect, leave or allow us so that we may follow you.

activation_trace.role: A separated piece turns the speakers into material detached from the moving whole.

changed_reading.before: A group left behind asks to catch up.
changed_reading.after: A self-separated piece asks to be grafted back onto the moving body only when that body reaches nourishment.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The packet's split mapping from the saying root into the smallness root makes this activation available, but it is form-distant and must not be presented as etymological identity. It remains anchored in four saying occurrences and the final smallness term; qualify it as a sound-and-branch tension between verbal abundance and cognitive scarcity.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Four occurrences of saying culminate in the statement that they understand only a little.

activation_trace.role: Prolific speech supplies the noisy abundance at one pole of the ayah.
The split-root image of instability makes repeated saying churn without settling into comprehension.
Explicit smallness supplies the cognitive scarcity at the other pole.
Instability keeps the little grasp they possess from organizing their many utterances.

changed_reading.before: They speak repeatedly despite understanding little.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an inverse economy: speech proliferates and oscillates precisely where comprehension is too slight to stabilize it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The admiration-without-removal branch is less expected under their accusation and does not erase the ordinary hostile sense. It remains anchored in the explicit envy root, their wish to follow, and the gain sought; downstream prose should frame it as reflexive irony in the accusation rather than a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: They accuse the addressed group of envy while themselves seeking the same acquired advantage.

activation_trace.role: Admiring another's advantage without wishing it removed exposes a possible mirror of the speakers' own desire.
Following supplies the imitative movement toward what the other group has.
Acquired advantage is the shared object around which accusation and imitation turn.
Attributing what is not so keeps the accusation available as projection.

changed_reading.before: They accuse the others of wanting their good withheld.
changed_reading.after: Their accusation may ironically project their own admiring wish to duplicate the others' advantage, turning the envy claim into a confession of imitative desire.

strongest_changes: Following became entry into a causal sequence, not mere shared movement; the rejected move is retroactive attachment at the yield-bearing end.

The exact gain-and-taking recurrence tied the disputed allocation to pledge, interior stabilization, recompense, and promise, so changing the word became extraction and reassignment of one segment from a larger bundle.
Hastened, unavailable-but-encompassed, and near-before-later fulfillments recoded the envy charge as a failure to understand phased access.
Repeated restraint of hands showed that victory can consist in controlled non-taking, displacing the focus speakers' acquisition-only metric.
The later no-substitution formula for God's running way expanded the threatened word into an executable and recurrent path.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah's dense speech contest and doubled following construction activated several coexisting mechanisms: covenant return, failed forecasting, temporal scheduling, protective boundary management, an adhered norm, and organic growth. The packet's split mappings also preserved form-distant readings in which speech oscillates against little understanding and the word retains a wound-like trace.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact scope of the prior divine word is not stated inside the focus ayah; the pledge, promise, affixed word, and running way may illuminate it without being identical to it.
The withheld-hands and hidden-body mechanisms are strong surah-level patterns, but their direct causal application to this particular refusal remains abductive.
The plant, severance, and wound models are materially coherent but should remain exploratory rather than displace the speech and allocation senses.
The split-root saying-to-smallness activation is packet-grounded but form-distant and should be treated as patterned resonance, not historical derivation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Opportunistic release into another’s track.** `انطلقتم` anchors ط ل ق B001/B003 (release from restraint; unrestrained going); `مغانم` anchors غ ن م B002 (gaining), `تأخذوها` ء خ ذ B001 (taking possession), and `نتبعكم` ت ب ع B001/B003 (following; stepwise tracking). This sudden mobility reverses their earlier rear-position. I infer that visible gain, not repaired allegiance, releases them. “Following” reads as entering an already-made track for extraction.
2. **Substitution aimed at an effective word.** `يبدلوا` anchors ب د ل B001/B002 (replacement/alteration); `كلام` anchors ك ل م B001/B002, meaningful speech; `من قبل` anchors ق ب ل B002, priorness. The attempted replacement is checked by an earlier utterance, anticipating the unchangeable `سنة` in 48:23. I infer that changing participation would functionally rewrite the prior allocation. Their request becomes an attempted alteration of operative speech, not merely a request for permission.
3. **Two envy readings remain distinct.** `تحسدوننا` anchors ح س د B001 (wanting another’s blessing removed) and B002 (emulative envy without dispossession). Under B001, they accuse the believers of exclusionary loss-making; under B002, they redescribe principled refusal as rivalry over gain. The packet does not choose between those accusations. `لا يفقهون` (ف ق ه B001) marks both as failures to grasp the prior-word mechanism.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 48:23 directly answers the attempted substitution with a running way that admits no replacement. Ayah 48:16 also corrects opportunistic following by issuing a new summons whose value lies in obedience, not gain.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Appetite-led flocking.** Fixed `مَغَانِم` activates غ ن م `B001`, the sheep or small-livestock flock, alongside gain in `B002`; fixed `نَتَّبِعْكُمْ` and `تَتَّبِعُونَا` activate ت ب ع `B007`, a calf following its mother, alongside ordinary following. Ayah 48:16 replaces gain with a severe summons, while 48:20 again names abundant gains as divinely staged. The packet supplies the attractor and the following motion; I infer **anticipated acquisition -> herd-like attachment to whoever reaches it**. Their proposed following reads as appetite-responsive flocking, distinct from covenantal allegiance.

2. **An attempted substitution into an already ordered utterance.** Fixed `يُبَدِّلُوا` anchors ب د ل `B001`, replacement or substitution, and `كَلَام` anchors ك ل م `B002`, a meaningful utterance extending to a saying. The fixed `مِن قَبْلُ` activates ق ب ل `B002`, priorness; 48:20 later shows a phased promise and one item brought forward. The packet gives prior wording and staged allocation; I infer **late self-insertion -> replacement of an assigned participant or phase**. The desired change is therefore practical role-substitution within the utterance's order, not only verbal editing.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 48:16 replaced the anticipated gains with severe resistance, exposing the appetite that powers the fixed following verbs. Ayah 48:20 then disclosed a staged promise, confirming that the requested late inclusion would substitute participants within an existing order.

baseline.text: Geride bırakılanlar, ganimetleri almak üzere yola çıktığınızda, “Bırakın, size uyalım” diyecekler. Allah'ın sözünü değiştirmek istiyorlar. De ki: “Bize asla uymayacaksınız. Allah daha önce böyle söyledi.” Bunun üzerine, “Hayır, bizi kıskanıyorsunuz” diyecekler. Aslında onlar pek az anlıyorlar.

findings.text: Kazanç görünür olunca öne çıkıp başkasının açtığı izi takip etme isteği, onarılmış bağlılıktan değil, elde etme fırsatından doğan seçici bir hareketliliktir.
Sonradan katılma talebi, önceden verilmiş sözün katılımcılarını ve aşamalarını fiilen değiştirerek onu yeniden yazma girişimidir.
İnananları kıskançlıkla suçlamak, ilkesel dışlamayı karşı tarafın onların payını yok etmek istemesi olarak yanlış tanımlar.
Aynı kıskançlık suçlaması, ilkesel reddi kazanç çevresindeki bir yarış olarak yeniden adlandırır.
Kazanç çevresinde toplanıp onu elde edene takılma isteğinde, sürünün iştahla peşine düşmesini çağrıştıran bir hareket de sezilebilir.

inter_ayah_rows.note: It supplies a fixed revelatory boundary across messengers, but not the contested prior directive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It closely parallels people who wait for victory and then claim association with the successful party.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It concerns receiving divine speech, without clarifying its alteration or the later request for gains.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It offers a pattern of return after temporary relief, only remotely related to the repeated conduct in 48:15.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It provides a distant parallel for refusing to follow incompatible directions after knowledge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: It does not materially illuminate 48:15.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It establishes a boundary against circulating false speech, a secondary check on the counteraccusation in 48:15.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It gives a generic division between saved followers and deniers, without a close relation to late participation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It supplies an ancestral excuse framed by “before,” but not the gain-seeking request or divine restriction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: It does not materially illuminate 48:15.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays following a prophet as falsely cast as loss, a distant parallel to the contest over motives and allegiance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It establishes that commanded fighting can be unwelcome despite its divinely known good, a broad backdrop to withdrawal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It records a group that requested fighting and then turned away when it was prescribed, closely paralleling conditional commitment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes those who seek the world from those who seek the hereafter during conflict, sharpening the gain-motive dimension.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It records people who decline battle while saying they would follow if they knew fighting, a close parallel to self-exculpating refusal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays a person who hangs back and treats absence from harm as favor, closely matching the earlier left-behind posture.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays the same delayed associate claiming that, had he been present when bounty came, he would have attained a great success.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes those who sit back, apart from those with injury, from those who strive with wealth and selves, clarifying the moral difference between incapacity and refusal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It assigns the spoils to God and the Messenger, directly grounding the non-claimability of gains.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It specifies that war gains have a divinely assigned distribution, supporting the principle that access is not self-determined.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It places taking gains within a divinely regulated conflict order rather than as an independent entitlement.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It permits enjoyment of gains only after the preceding divine regulation, providing a secondary limit on acquisition.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It rebukes those who remain fixed when told to go forth in God's way, a close antecedent to being left behind.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands going forth whether lightly or heavily equipped, contrasting with selective participation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It says that an easy, near gain would have drawn their following, but a difficult journey kept them back, closely exposing conditional allegiance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It says that had they truly intended departure they would have prepared, but they were held back and told to remain with those who remain.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It records an excuse for not going forth, supplying a close parallel to the self-protective speech of the left-behind.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays people satisfied only when given from a distribution and angered when denied, a direct material-interest parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It contrasts demanding a share with contentment in what God and His Messenger give.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It bars a group from going forth again because they first preferred to sit back, closely paralleling exclusion after earlier nonparticipation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It records wealthy people asking leave to remain with those who sit when striving is commanded.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes excusing Bedouins and those who sit back, adding a nearby taxonomy of absence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It fixes blame on the affluent who ask permission to stay back and are content to be with those who remain.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It says surrounding believers should not stay behind God's Messenger or prefer themselves to him, directly defining the violated priority.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It describes people who profess belief and obedience but then have a party turn away, a close speech-and-conduct parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It shows a party turning away when called to God and the Messenger for judgment, supporting the pattern of selective compliance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It contrasts their turning away with their coming submissively when judgment appears to favor them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It provides the opposing model: believers answer a summons to judgment with hearing and obedience.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies those who hinder others and call them away from the Messenger while themselves scarcely coming to battle.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays people as miserly toward the believers and panic-stricken at danger, supplying a secondary contrast to costly commitment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts people who expect danger and would rather remain among the Bedouins asking news than participate.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It contrasts the stated desire for a command with fear when a decisive command for fighting is sent down.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies obedience and fitting speech as better when the matter becomes determined, reinforcing the failure of declared readiness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It gives greater rank to those who spent and fought before the opening than to those who did so later, strongly supporting the significance of prior participation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It assigns fay to God, the Messenger, and designated purposes, supporting the principle of governed distribution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly makes the Messenger's allotment determinative and prevents wealth from circulating only among the rich, directly relevant to disputed entitlement.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies an early recipient group for fay by displacement and striving, a secondary parallel to priority shaped by prior cost.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays believers who do not find need for what others receive and who prefer them despite need, a direct ethical contrast to demanding access.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It records a promise of joint departure and nonobedience to opponents that is not fulfilled, a secondary parallel to unreliable allegiance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It states that those promising support will neither go out nor render aid, confirming the unreliability of their declared participation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts people dispersing toward commerce and leaving the Messenger standing, a distant parallel to preferring immediate material opportunity.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts people turning away when told to come for forgiveness, supplying a secondary parallel to resistant posture after speech.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A summons reorganizes bodies by launching them toward an encounter, resolving contact, or exposing reversal and refusal.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The people named by the summons carry a latent rising function, so mobilization begins before combat in the conversion of a stationary group into an undertaking.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Summons Launches Following
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A call raises a group into action, releases departure, and draws followers into the same movement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: summons or call (`quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`); rising to an undertaking (`quranic:root_001273:B003/m01`); following (`quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`); catching up with a leader (`quranic:root_000175:B002/m01`); launch or unimpeded departure (`quranic:root_000946:B003/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:16 `ستدعون` and `قوم` (د ع و; ق و م); 48:15 `انطلقتم`, `نتبعكم`, and `تتبعونا` (ط ل ق; ت ب ع).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The call is a kinetic event. It makes the group-root perform its latent rising action, opens a departure path, and tests whether those behind will genuinely enter and maintain the leader's trajectory.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A summons reorganizes bodies by launching them toward an encounter, resolving contact, or exposing reversal and refusal.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The people named by the summons carry a latent rising function, so mobilization begins before combat in the conversion of a stationary group into an undertaking.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Remaining Behind Becomes Reversal
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Refusal leaves a party behind and then turns movement backward at the point of pressure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: those remaining behind (`quranic:root_000433:B003/m01`); turning away (`quranic:root_001684:B007/m01`); turning the back in retreat (`quranic:root_000458:B003/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:15 `المخلفون` and 48:16 `المخلفين` (خ ل ف); 48:16 `تتولوا` and 48:22 `يولون` (و ل ي); 48:22 `الأدبار` (د ب ر).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Being left behind is not only a location in the marching order. Under renewed summons it becomes an orientation: refusal turns the body away, and military retreat makes that orientation visible as the exposed back.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A valid form remains effective by resisting replacement, whether it is spoken, traveled, or fastened as an obligation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Speech, precedent, and obligation share the same preservation mechanism even though one is uttered, one is traversed, and one adheres to persons.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: A Spoken Directive Resists Editing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An uttered claim attempts to alter a prior directive, but the word remains unavailable for substitution.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: voiced utterance (`quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`); substitution (`quranic:root_000095:B001/m01`); change or replacement (`quranic:root_000095:B002/m01`); word as articulated unit (`quranic:root_001316:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:15 `سيقول`, `يريدون أن يبدلوا`, `كلام`, `لن تتبعونا`, and `قال` (ق و ل; ب د ل; ك ل م).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The later speech proposes an edit to an already operative word. The substitution root exposes the attempt as replacement rather than interpretation, while the word-root preserves the directive as a bounded form.
